answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a prism, before it can post or attest. A single trellis checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 478 aliases hence costs 370 bonds held for 19 days each, plus the lantern attestations those aliases can never earn. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
